scores.evidence: Transactions the existing engine declined are evaluated separately, because they never get outcome labels
scores.rationale: Technical claims are accurate throughout, including subtle areas (reject inference, PCI scope via QSA-confirmed tokenization, out-of-time evaluation, idempotent replay), with limits stated honestly as assumptions.

scores.evidence: I assumed we're the card issuer (or its processor) and that we score each authorization before it's approved or declined.
scores.rationale: Solves the exact problem inline-real-time with explicit resolution of ambiguities (issuer vs acquirer, brownfield), credible phasing, and explicit justified deferrals in §10.

scores.evidence: The auth host stays the system of record for decisions, and existing case management for cases
scores.rationale: Clear ownership of every component and data item, decisions made once (sync, fallback, tokenization) are honored consistently across phases, validations and cross-cutting tables with no contradictions.

scores.evidence: Out-of-time backtest (train on earlier months, test on the last 3); existing-engine declines analyzed separately
scores.rationale: V0–V9 tie checks to the specific risks, thresholds are explicitly labeled ASSUMPTION rather than invented, riskiest items (PAN boundary, latency, uplift) validate before commitment, and V9/drift monitoring continue post-launch.

scores.evidence: Peak is a BASELINE, measured in Phase 0. 3× is an ASSUMPTION: headroom for attack bursts and growth
scores.rationale: Every number is tagged ASSUMPTION/BASELINE/UNKNOWN, missing inputs are listed with owners and deadlines, and each key assumption states what changes if it is wrong.

scores.evidence: Game day: forced bad threshold, scorer killed, corrupt model artifact; in shadow first
scores.rationale: Covers the hardest domain failures mass false declines, PAN leakage, scorer outage, duplicates/replays, label poisoning, adversarial input, corrupt artifacts each with concrete detection (breaker, DLP) and recovery (fallback, rebuild drill).

scores.evidence: Rollback: per-segment flag back to the existing engine within seconds; the breaker reverts automatically.
scores.rationale: Deploy/rollback mechanics, meaningful signals (fallback rate, would-decline rate, drift), on-call rota, runbooks, and an explicit operational-complexity budget sized to one team are designed in from Phase 0.

scores.evidence: Run cost per 1k scored transactions | Ceiling UNKNOWN. Finance supplies it in Phase 1 alongside the uplift bar
scores.rationale: Cost is a gated budget with a per-transaction unit metric and build-vs-buy economics, and no figures are invented, but the concrete cost drivers (store, stream compute) and their growth are not enumerated.

scores.evidence: R3. Feature history, training data and the decision log are all keyed on it
scores.rationale: Each decision carries an explicit reversibility class, the R3 ones (PAN boundary, schema, build-vs-buy, fail mode) are validated earliest, and every row has a revisit trigger and exit path.

scores.evidence: One scoring service (feature fetch, rules and model in one process) and one Flink job
scores.rationale: Starts with the simplest latency-safe design, justifies each component, and defers speculative complexity (multi-region, graph models, per-segment models) behind concrete pull-forward triggers.

scores.evidence: V4 fails: flip to async for alerts only, and keep the existing engine inline
scores.rationale: A concrete Phase 0 slice, dependency-justified ordering, per-phase exit checks, named technology defaults, and explicit contingency branches mean a team could start immediately.

checklist.evidence: p99 ≤ 50 ms, hard timeout 80 ms, then fall back to the existing engine
R3. Minutes of fail-closed means mass declines; fail-open during an attack means losses
One feature-definition repo that generates both the Flink (online) and Spark (offline, point-in-time) jobs.
Label pipeline: confirmed fraud claims and fraud chargeback reason codes, with label-maturity windows.
Uplift ≥ the V3 bar at an equal would-decline rate; would-be false declines ≤ the existing engine's BASELINE
hard rules (e.g. blocked card) override; score bands map to approve / step-up / decline / approve+alert.
Analyst dispositions enter the labels only through review.
Tokenize the PAN in the auth-host adapter inside the CDE (keyed HMAC, key in the HSM/KMS).
Idempotency key: the network trace ID ... consumers keyed by trace ID so replays don't double-count
Shadow first, then per-segment champion/challenger, with the existing engine kept as fallback.
Response: score, recommended decision, reason codes, model version and config version ... decision log with the feature vector
Load test with a production-sized store at 3× peak for 1 h, plus a 15-min burst at 5× peak

traps.evidence: Synchronous inline scoring with a hard timeout.
Hard timeout and fallback to the existing engine.
Out-of-time backtest (train on earlier months, test on the last 3)
The pipeline sees only the token, the BIN and the last 4 digits, and never detokenizes

note: An exceptionally strong plan: inline scoring with real degraded modes, PCI scope control, leakage-free evaluation, and labeled assumptions throughout; only cost-driver enumeration is comparatively thin.
